facts.fact: The conference paper states that the electronic Egyptian Birth and Death Registration System (EBDRS), implemented in 2017, registers births and deaths, with causes of death, in a digitised system meant to replace the paper-based one, and that it registered 6,082 newborn refugees in 2017.
facts.system: Egyptian Birth and Death Registration System (EBDRS)

facts.fact: The paper states that data entry is done at the health office, which prints the birth or death registration certificate once entry is complete, that the offices are linked online to a central database over a secured GPRS/3G mobile network, and that registration is completed within 15 minutes against one month on paper; the system dates from 2017.
facts.system: Egyptian Birth and Death Registration System (EBDRS)

facts.fact: The paper states that EBDRS was developed and implemented in 2017 to automate 4,571 health offices, 300 health departments and 27 health directorates and link them to a central database, by the account of the Ministry of Planning, Monitoring and Administrative Reform; it gives no total number of health offices against the 4,571.
facts.system: Egyptian Birth and Death Registration System (EBDRS)

facts.fact: The paper states that the Ministry of Planning, Monitoring and Administrative Reform developed and implemented EBDRS in 2017 in collaboration with the Ministry of Health, in whose system the registration is held, under the existing Civil Registration Act with no change in the law.
facts.system: Egyptian Birth and Death Registration System (EBDRS)

systems.system: EBDRS electronic notification to the civil registration authority and links to other services
systems.tiers: the Ministry of Health electronically notifies the civil registration authority of new vital events; interoperability serves identity management and universal health insurance, and updates the population clock at CAPMAS

note: Classed civil because the paper says the health office is where the event is entered and the registration certificate printed; it also says the Ministry of Health then notifies the civil registration authority electronically, so the parent may read the health office as a notifier instead. No publication date is printed; facts are dated to 2017, the year the paper gives for implementation. No finance source is stated.
